catalysts: Cu/ZnO-based catalyst systems; formulation is process-specific
technologies.process_conditions: Elevated pressure and temperature; report the specific reactor conditions rather than a universal optimum.

technical_performance.assumptions: Complete atom balance; excludes losses and purge

technologies.demonstrated_scale: Project-dependent. No plant-level scale or operational status has been verified in this initial atlas.
known_limitations: Water separation, purge losses and heat integration
technologies.economics: Purchased hydrogen can dominate feedstock cost. Use the transparent scenario model; its partial cost excludes capital recovery and fixed operating expenses.
technologies.lifecycle_evidence: Carbon in fuel is released at use. Climate benefit depends on feedstock origin, displaced production and energy supply; utilization does not establish removal.

chemical_reactions: CO₂ + 2 H⁺ + 2 e⁻ → CO + H₂O (cathode half-reaction)
products: CO or other products, depending on catalyst and reactor
catalysts: Silver-based systems for CO; copper-based systems for multicarbon products
technologies.process_conditions: Specify electrolyte, full-cell voltage, current density, electrode area and operating duration together.
technologies.demonstrated_scale: Laboratory and larger systems must be assessed individually; no universal pathway TRL is assigned.
technologies.economics: Faradaic efficiency alone does not specify electricity consumption: full-cell voltage, current and production rate are needed.
technologies.lifecycle_evidence: Include electricity and replacement materials; track carbon leaving every outlet, not only the desired product.

catalysts: No universal catalyst; mineral reactivity and conditioning control the process
technologies.process_conditions: Pressure, moisture and particle size depend on feedstock and product route.
technologies.demonstrated_scale: Route-specific; curing, aggregate production and waste treatment cannot share one readiness rating.
technologies.economics: Consider feedstock treatment, CO₂ delivery, product value and local transport rather than carbon uptake alone.
technologies.lifecycle_evidence: Carbonate retention may be durable, but net removal additionally requires atmospheric carbon and a complete lifecycle balance. Calcining virgin limestone can offset carbonation uptake.
